working_title: Northumberland's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Bamburgh, Dunstanburgh, Seahouses and Goswick
angle: Northumberland has a string of genuine links courses running from Embleton Bay up to the Scottish border that remain far less crowded and far cheaper than their East Lothian neighbours just an hour to the north. The post maps the four main coastal courses as a logical trip itinerary, with honest notes on what each course is actually like to play and the practical details a visiting golfer needs.
research_notes:
- Northumberland coast has around 6 true links courses; the four headline coastal stops are Bamburgh Castle, Dunstanburgh Castle, Seahouses, and Goswick (Berwick-upon-Tweed)
- GOSWICK LINKS: Founded 1890, designed by James Braid, later modified by Frank Pennink. Stretches to around 6,800 yards, par 72. Ranked in the top 50 courses in England (National Club Golfer) and top 100 links in GB&I (Golf World). Has been an R&A Regional Qualifying venue for The Open Championship. Pure fescue links, firm and fast-running year-round. Two 9-hole loops both return to the clubhouse. Visitors welcome weekdays and after ~10am weekends; handicap certificate required, advance booking essential. Green fees quoted variously as £55–£110 depending on source/time of day (morning slots costliest); sources are inconsistent so describe as 'in the higher bracket for the region' rather than citing a firm figure. Five miles south of Berwick-upon-Tweed. Mackenzie & Ebert engaged for course improvement work (recent).
- BAMBURGH CASTLE GC: Opened 1904, designed by George Rochester. 18 holes, par 68, around 5,600 yards from white tees. Short but tricky; starts with two par 3s followed by two par 5s — unusual routing. Views to Bamburgh Castle (Grade I listed, 11th century), Lindisfarne, the Farne Islands and the Cheviots. No pro shop; logo'd clothing available from the bar. Hire clubs, trolleys and buggies available. Clubhouse has bar and food. Open to visitors every day. Visitor reviews note it feels expensive for what it is and that value-conscious visitors may prefer Dunstanburgh or Goswick. Undulating with blind shots — worth reading the course planner first visit.
- DUNSTANBURGH CASTLE GC: Links first established 1900, redesigned by James Braid. Wraps around Embleton Bay. National Trust land (maintained by club staff). Course Rating 71.2. Ranked 99th best course in England (source: dunstanburgh.com). Signature par 3 played over a ravine with the ruined castle on the horizon. Clubhouse refurbishment completed late 2025/early 2026. Widely praised as the best-value round on the coast. Located between Craster and Embleton village (Sea Lane, Embleton, NE66 3XQ). Within easy reach of Newcastle and the East Lothian golf coast.
- SEAHOUSES GC: Founded 1913 as 9-hole, expanded to 18 holes in 1976. Par 67, under 5,600 yards. Compact clifftop links within the Northumberland Coast AONB, 7 miles from the A1. Known for two iconic par 3s: 10th (tee shot entirely over water) and 15th (played over cliffs). Course of two distinct halves — inland fairways with water hazards on first nine, exposed coastal holes on second. Visitors welcome every day; advance booking essential. Green fees £22.50–£44 for 18 holes (from club's own website — most affordable on the coast). Dog-friendly on course, veranda, patio and bar. GolfMark accredited.
- LOGISTICS: Newcastle is roughly 1 hour south; Edinburgh roughly 1 hour 45 minutes north. All four courses drivable as a 2–3 night trip. Accommodation hubs: Bamburgh village, Seahouses, Alnwick, or Berwick-upon-Tweed. Northumberland Coast is an AONB.
- TONE NOTE: Reviewers consistently flag Goswick and Dunstanburgh as the most purely satisfying links tests; Bamburgh wins on scenery but splits opinion on value; Seahouses is the friendly, affordable warm-up option.
